screening_decisions.reason: Randomized trial comparing indomethacin (non-selective COX inhibitor) with terbutaline for tocolysis in women with preterm labor at 26-32 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria.
Observational pharmacokinetic study measuring indomethacin levels in maternal/fetal serum and amniotic fluid. Not a randomized trial of tocolysis; no intervention arm for treating preterm labor.
Cochrane review about magnesium sulphate for neuroprotection, not a primary randomized trial of COX inhibitors for tocolysis. Wrong intervention and wrong study type.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial comparing celecoxib (COX-2 selective inhibitor) with indomethacin (non-selective COX inhibitor) for treatment of preterm labor at 24-34 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized double-blind trial comparing sulindac (COX inhibitor) with terbutaline for management of preterm labor at approximately 32 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria.
Systematic review/meta-analysis about progestational agents, not COX inhibitors. Wrong intervention and wrong study type (review, not primary RCT).
Methodological paper about statistical analysis methods for trials with multiple pregnancies. Not a primary clinical trial of any intervention for preterm labor.

Prospective randomized double-blind trial comparing ritodrine+placebo vs ritodrine+indomethacin (COX inhibitor) for threatened preterm labor. Meets selection criteria as it tests COX inhibitor for tocolysis.
Randomized double-blind double-dummy trial comparing indomethacin (COX inhibitor) with nylidrin for imminent preterm labor at 25-34 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria.
Matched cohort study (not randomized) comparing neonatal outcomes in infants whose mothers received indomethacin vs those who did not. Wrong study design - not a randomized trial.
Methodological/statistical paper about analysis methods for trials with multiple births. Not a primary clinical trial of COX inhibitors for tocolysis.

While this is a randomized trial of rofecoxib (COX-2 inhibitor), it was for PROPHYLACTIC/preventive use in women at high risk, not for tocolysis in women IN LABOUR. Treatment started at 16 weeks before labor onset. Does not meet the 'women in labour' criterion.

Randomized double-masked trial of indomethacin (COX inhibitor) vs placebo for tocolysis in women with PPROM at 24-31 weeks gestation. Although PPROM is a specific condition, these women are in preterm labor and receive tocolysis. Meets selection criteria.
Randomized trial comparing two COX inhibitors (indomethacin vs sulindac) for refractory preterm labor at approximately 29-30 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized trial but enrolled women with LOW-RISK PREGNANCY and NO SIGNS OF PRETERM LABOR. The study tested effects on fetal movements in healthy pregnancies, not tocolysis in women in preterm labor. Does not meet population criterion.
Prospective randomized double-blind trial comparing indomethacin (COX inhibitor) with placebo for premature labor. Meets all selection criteria.
Prospective randomized trial comparing ketorolac (non-selective COX inhibitor) with magnesium sulfate for arrest of preterm labor at ≤32 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria.
Systematic review and network meta-analysis, not a primary randomized trial. Wrong study type.
Cochrane review about betamimetics, not COX inhibitors. Wrong intervention and wrong study type (review, not primary RCT).
Randomized prospective trial comparing indomethacin (COX inhibitor) with ritodrine for long-term treatment of preterm labor at 23-34 weeks gestation. Meets all selection criteria.
